source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the 2026 announcement table reads '5 February (MPR) · 19 March · 30 April (MPR) · 18 June · 30 July (MPR) · 17 September · 5 November (MPR) · 17 December', and the 5 November row reads verbatim 'Thursday 5 November — November MPC Summary and minutes and November Monetary Policy Report'. The same fetch returns the 2027 PROVISIONAL list (4 Feb MPR · 18 Mar · 29 Apr MPR · 17 Jun · 29 Jul MPR · 16 Sep · 4 Nov MPR · 16 Dec). The 12:00 London publication time is corroborated by the Bank's own page-title convention for a forecast round — the July 2026 MPR page published as 'Monetary Policy Report - July 2026 (to be published at 12pm)' — rather than by a stated time on the dates page. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has FED: and no slot for a non-Fed central bank — the same gap boe-decision-2026-09-17, ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and boj-decision-2026-09-18 were filed under. notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/boe-decision-2026-11-05.from-boe-decision-2026-09-17.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). That proposal's placement finding stands and is kept: this is the venue where the September ledger's terminal-rate call is adjudicated, it is the first MPC meeting AFTER the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget and its OBR forecast, and the strip on 2026-09-08 put 54.2% on a higher rate here against 93.1% hold on 09-17. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED: this is the ONLY genuinely two-sided rate decision on the UK strip — 54.2% hike / 45.9% hold / 0.0% cut, implied 3.89% (centralbank.watch, fetched 2026-09-09, data as-of 09-08) — while September is a 93.1% settled hold and December is 94.6% CUMULATIVE, i.e. conditional on this meeting. And three independent reads contradict that price: the Bank's OWN Market Participants Survey (BoE primary, fetched; 15-17 July 2026, 78 respondents) has an end-2026 median of 3.75% with over 90% on hold after July, then CUTS to 3.50% / 3.25% / 3.25% at the one-, two- and three-year horizons; a Reuters poll of 64 economists (13-18 August 2026) has 56 of 64 expecting no change for the rest of 2026, six a hike and two a cut; and the July 2026 MPR's own modal path — CPI peaking 3.2% in Q4 2026, then 1.7% at the two-year horizon (Q1 2028) and 1.9% at three (Q3 2029) — UNDERSHOOTS the target while conditioned on a market curve carrying roughly two hikes by Q3 2027. September has no forecast round; November is where that arithmetic gets refreshed and published, which is why the MPR is this meeting's payload exactly as the annual QT review is September's. There is NO balance-sheet decision here: the 19 June 2026 APF market notice puts the annual gilt-reduction review at the 17 September meeting. Tiered medium and NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: symbols: [], no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the only route to this book is the second-order global-term-premium channel fomc-2026-09-16 already owns. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
